title: Roll a maki with a bamboo mat, seam side down, then open the mat
instruction: Use the bamboo mat to roll the rice-covered nori sheet round the green cucumber, seam side down, then open the mat flat and let go.
context: Making sushi at home is a familiar kitchen scene: home sushi kits come with a makisu, a mat of bamboo slats strung side by side so it bends like a chain of hinges, and the same mat rolls kimbap and other filled rolls. The mat is the tool: both hands lift its near edge and curl it up behind and over the filling, then feed it forward so the roll turns inside the curl and winds the rice-covered nori round itself, tight. The mat is then peeled back off the finished roll, which must stay closed with its seam underneath, where the roll's weight holds it. As in any kitchen, the hands touch only the mat, not the ready-to-eat rice.
setup: Station table; positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, x forward (away from the robot), y to the robot's left. (1) Butcher block: oiled end-grain maple, 28.0 x 19.0 x 10.0 cm (a standard 4-inch block), 3.7 kg, light brown, fixed to the table from x 24.5 to 52.5 cm, y -9.5 to +9.5 cm. (2) Sushi mat (makisu): 24 bamboo slats, each 0.9 x 24.0 x 0.3 cm and 4.5 g (108 g in all), alternating light and darker tan, bound with cotton string every 1.0 cm; flat on the block with the slats running left-right, near edge at x 26.55 cm, far edge at x 50.45 cm, centred on y 0, so each slat end overhangs the block by 2.5 cm. (3) Sheet of nori spread thinly with sushi rice and cut to one turn round the cucumber, rice side (white) up, nori side (dark green) down: 19.0 x 8.76 cm, 1.7 mm thick, 33 g; flat on the mat from x 33.12 to 41.88 cm, centred on y 0. (4) Japanese cucumber, green, ends trimmed: 2.6 cm across, 18.0 cm long, 95 g; pressed into the rice along the sheet's near edge, its axis along y at x 33.5 cm, centred on y 0.
scoring: Scored at the end of the run; success is 1.0 held for 1 s. Gates first, each scores 0: the cucumber was lifted more than 2 cm at any time; it left the block area (x outside 25 to 52 cm or more than 6 cm off centre) at any time; a gripper pad came within 4 mm of the rice, nori or cucumber at any time (hands off the food); when the sheet first covered 180 deg of the cucumber, the mat had not been curled at least 120 deg (slat 0 turned over relative to the far slat), so the mat did not do the rolling; the grippers have not been at least 3 cm from the mat and the food, with the grippers, the mat and the roll still (under 1 cm/s), for the last 1 s. These whole-run records are kept every control step and cleared only by the simulator reset. Ladder, on the state at the end: 0.25 if the sheet covers at least 180 deg of the cucumber; 0.5 if at least 300 deg; 0.75 if at least 330 deg, its outer edge lies on the roll within 60 deg of straight down (seam side down) and the cucumber is square to the table edge within 10 deg; 1.0 if also the mat lies open (no hinge bent over 20 deg, no slat over 10 mm above flat) with the roll on it. Wrap = the arc covered by the longest run of consecutive 8 mm sheet strips lying 12.5 to 17.5 mm from the cucumber's axis. Real check: lift the roll and look at its underside (far edge underneath, meeting the near edge), lay a straightedge on the mat, and take a top photo showing both grippers 3 cm clear.
reset_notes: Block flush with a tape line 24.5 cm in front of the arm-base line, centred on the arms' midline. Lay the mat flat, slats across the table, near edge on a tape mark at x 26.55 cm, centred. Spread a fresh sheet with rice, cut to 8.76 cm, and lay it rice side up with its near edge on a tape tick at x 33.12 cm (6.57 cm in from the mat's near edge), centred. Press a trimmed cucumber into the rice along the near edge, its axis over a tick at x 33.5 cm. Use fresh food for every trial.
fidelity: The rice-covered nori is 11 rigid 8 mm strips (0.5 mm nori under 1.2 mm rice, 3 g each) hinged with a weak spring to flat, cut to one turn so its edges meet without overlap; the edge strip ends in a 31 deg ramp. Rice tack: the cucumber is welded to that strip; elsewhere tack is friction only. The soft roll's rolling resistance is angular damping (150/s) on the cucumber. The cucumber is rigid; the mat's binding is a free hinge.
